passages.title: Age of Exploration
passages.text:
The Age of Exploration started in the 1400's. Europeans were desperate to get spices from Asia. Spices were used to preserve foods and keep them from spoiling. Spices, however, were expensive and dangerous to get. European rulers began to pay for explorations to find a sea route to Asia so they could get spices cheaper. Portugal was the first country that sent explorers to search for the sea route to Asia. After Bartholomew Dias and his crew made it to Africa's Cape of Good Hope, Vasco da Gama and his crew became the first to sail around Africa and through the Indian Ocean to India in 1497. Spain, however, would soon take over the lead in exploration. When Portugal refused to finance Christopher Columbus' idea to sail west to find the shortcut to the Indies, Columbus convinced Spain's King Ferdinand and Queen Isabella to finance it. On October 12, 1492, Christopher Columbus and his crew reached the island of Hispaniola. Although Columbus believed he had reached Asia, he had actually discovered the entire continent of North America and claimed it for Spain.

Spain quickly colonized North America. Ponce de Leon discovered Florida, and the first European settlement in the New World was later established at St. Augustine. Hernando Cortes crushed the Aztec empire in Mexico and claimed it for Spain. Francisco Pizarro did the same to the Incan Empire in South America. Other explorers such as Francisco Coronado and Hernando de Soto claimed other portions of North America for Spain. Vasco Nunez de Balboa even claimed the entire Pacific Ocean for Spain. As the Spanish empire grew, explorers forced native populations into slavery and to convert to Christianity. Meanwhile, France began to explore North America. Explorations by Giovanni Verrazano and Jacques Cartier resulted in French claims of much of Canada and the north Atlantic coast. England would soon attempt to make its presence known by financing pirates such as Francis Drake to raid Spanish settlements and steal gold from Spanish sea vessels. England also established a settlement in North Carolina in 1587. Territorial disputes and constant pirating resulted in a series of major wars between the competing nations. In 1588, the British Army defeated the vaunted Spanish Armada. The British victory proved a serious blow to Spanish influence in the New World.

Although Spain still controlled much of the New World after defeat, England and France were able to accelerate their colonization. England soon established successful colonies throughout the eastern portions of the United States, and France had colonies in Canada and the middle portions of the United States. By the mid 1700's, new territorial disputes between England and France eventually resulted in England gaining control over much of North America after the French and Indian War. English colonies flourished in North America until 1776 when the colonists declared their independence. The Revolutionary War ensued and resulted in independence for the colonists. The United States of America was formed.

questions.q: What country was the first to send explorers to search for a sea route to Asia?
questions.explanation: Portugal sent explorers first — Dias reached the Cape of Good Hope and da Gama sailed to India in 1497. Spain, France and England all followed later.

questions.q: Who was the first explorer to sail through the Indian Ocean to India?
questions.explanation: Da Gama rounded Africa and crossed the Indian Ocean to India in 1497. Columbus sailed west in 1492, Balboa claimed the Pacific, and Cortes conquered Mexico.

questions.q: Christopher Columbus believed he had reached the ---.
questions.explanation: The passage says Columbus believed he had reached Asia, i.e. the Indies. Spain financed him, and North America is what he actually found.

questions.q: Which country wasn't claimed by Spain?
questions.explanation: Canada was claimed by France through Verrazano and Cartier. Spain claimed Florida, the Pacific Ocean and South America.

questions.q: What country established the first permanent European settlement in the New World?
questions.explanation: St. Augustine, the first permanent European settlement, was Spanish. England's settlement came in 1587 and France held Canada.

questions.q: What happened first?
options: Vasco da Gama sails to India
Vasco Nunez de Balboa claims the Pacific Ocean for Spain
questions.explanation: Columbus reached Hispaniola on 12 October 1492. Da Gama's voyage was 1497, and Ponce de Leon and Balboa came after that.

questions.q: What happened last?
options: The English establish a settlement in North Carolina
Vasco Nunez de Balboa discovers the Pacific Ocean
questions.explanation: The Revolutionary War began in 1776. The Armada defeat (1588), the North Carolina settlement (1587) and Balboa's claim (1513) all came earlier.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes why the Age of Exploration occurred?
options: England and Spain wanted to expand their empires
Spain had claimed North and South America
European rulers wanted to find a cheaper way to obtain spices from Asia
The English defeated the Spanish Armada
questions.explanation: Rulers paid for explorations to find a sea route to Asia so spices would be cheaper. Empire-building, Spanish claims and the Armada were results or later events, not causes.

questions.q: Which of the following is true?
options: The English defeated the Spanish Armada in 1587
Vasco da Gama claimed the Pacific Ocean for Spain
Hernando Cortes conquered the Incan empire in South America
Explorations by Giovanni Verrazano and Jacques Cartier resulted in French claims of much of Canada
questions.explanation: Verrazano and Cartier's voyages gave France much of Canada. The Armada was 1588, Balboa (not da Gama) claimed the Pacific, and Cortes conquered the Aztecs, not the Incas.

questions.q: Which of the following is false?
options: Sir Francis Drake was an English pirate
Spain was the first country to search for a sea route to Asia
Spices were used to preserve food
Vasco da Gama sailed for Portugal.
questions.explanation: Portugal, not Spain, was first to search for the sea route to Asia — so that statement is false. The other three are all true in the passage.

passages.title: Cheating and Plagiarism
passages.text:
Students are responsible for familiarizing themselves with the University Code of Student Conduct, as on the enrolment with the University the students have placed themselves under the policies and regulations of the University and all of its duly constituted bodies. Disciplinary authority is exercised through the Student Conduct Committee. The Committee has procedures in place for hearing allegations of misconduct. Copies of the Student Conduct Code are available at the Student Services Office.

Academic dishonesty is never condoned by the University. This includes cheating and plagiarism, which violate the Student Conduct Code and could result in expulsion or failing the course. Cheating includes but is not limited to obtaining or giving unauthorized help during an examination, getting unauthorized information about the contents of an examination before it is administered, using unauthorized sources of information during an examination, altering or falsifying the record of any grades, altering or supplying answers after an examination has been handed in, falsifying any official University record, and misrepresenting the facts to get exemptions from or extensions to course requirements.

Plagiarism includes but is not limited to submitting any paper or other document, to satisfy an academic requirement, which has been copied either in whole or in part from someone else's work without identifying that person, failing to identify as a quotation a documented idea that has not been thoroughly assimilated into the student's language and style, or paraphrasing a passage so closely that the reader could be misled as to the source, submitting the same written or oral material in different courses without obtaining authorization from the lecturers involved, or 'dry-labbing' which includes obtaining and using experimental data from fellow students without the expressed consent of the lecturer, utilizing experimental data and laboratory write-ups from other parts of the course or from previous terms during which the course was conducted, and fabricating data to fit the expected results.

questions.q: Upon enrollment, students are to:
options: Familiarize themselves with the university's policies & regulations.
questions.explanation: On enrolment students come under the University's rules, so they must familiarize themselves with the Code of Student Conduct. Students cannot negotiate these rules.

questions.q: The role exercised by the Student Conduct Committee is to:
questions.explanation: The Committee hears allegations of misconduct and exercises disciplinary authority — not general complaints, suggestions or admissions.

questions.q: In paragraph II, the word 'condoned' is closer to the meaning of which phrasal verb?
questions.explanation: 'Condoned' means tolerated or accepted, which matches 'put up with'. 'Put down/aside/out' mean suppress, save and extinguish.

questions.q: Academic dishonesty includes:
questions.explanation: The passage states academic dishonesty includes cheating and plagiarism. Class absence and dropping out are not academic dishonesty.

questions.q: Cheating includes all the following EXCEPT:
options: Getting and giving unauthorized exam content information before exams.
Giving answers after an exam is handed in
questions.explanation: Study circles are not listed as cheating. Unauthorized exam info, altering grades and supplying answers after the exam are all explicitly listed.

questions.q: What does the author mean by 'dry-labbing'?
options: Obtaining, using or altering unauthorized experimental data
Making sure that the lab is dry
questions.explanation: Dry-labbing is using fellow students' data without consent, reusing old lab write-ups, or fabricating data. Quotation errors are plagiarism, and lab hygiene is a literal misreading.

questions.q: Altering facts to get exemptions or extensions is considered as an act of plagiarism.
questions.explanation: Misrepresenting facts for exemptions or extensions is listed under cheating, not plagiarism — so the statement is false.

questions.q: The text emphasizes the importance of obtaining the lecturer's consent when submitting written or oral material.
questions.explanation: Submitting the same written or oral material in different courses without the lecturers' authorization is explicitly listed as plagiarism — so the statement is true.

questions.q: Paraphrasing is academically unacceptable.
questions.explanation: False. Only paraphrasing so closely that the reader could be misled as to the source is plagiarism; a properly credited paraphrase is acceptable.

questions.q: Committing either cheating or plagiarism doesn't lead to expulsion or course failure.
questions.explanation: False. The passage states these violations could result in expulsion or failing the course.

passages.title: Amazon Rain Forest
passages.text:
The Amazon is the world's largest tropical rain forest. It covers an area of nearly 2.8 million square miles, which is nearly the size of the continent of Australia. The Amazon rain forest gets its life from the majestic Amazon River, the world's second-largest river, which runs directly through the heart of the region. The rain forest itself is simply the drainage basin for the river and its many tributaries. The vast forest itself consists of four layers, each featuring its own ecosystems and specially adapted plants and animals.

The forest floor is the lowest region. Since only 2 percent of the sunlight filters through the top layers to the understory, very few plants grow here. The forest floor, however, is rich with rotting vegetation and the bodies of dead organisms, which are quickly broken down into nutrients integrated into the soil. Tree roots stay close to these available nutrients, and decomposers, such as millipedes and earthworms, use these nutrients for food.

The understory is the layer above the forest floor. Much like the forest floor, only about 2-5 percent of the sunlight reaches this shadowy realm. Many of the plants in the understory have large, broad leaves to collect as much sunlight as possible. The understory is so thick that there is very little air movement. As a result, plants rely on insects and animals to pollinate their flowers.

The layer above the understory is the canopy. This is where much of the action in the rain forest occurs. Many canopy leaves have specially adapted leaves which form 'drip tips.' Drip tips allow water to flow off the leaves, which prevents mosses, fungi, and lichens from occupying the leaves. Leaves in the canopy are very dense and filter about 80 percent of the sunlight. The canopy is where the wealth of the rain forest's fruits and flowers grow. Bromeliads, cuplike plants, provide drinking pools for animals and breeding locations for tree frogs.

The emergent layer is above the canopy and is the top layer of the rain forest. Trees in the emergent layer break through the canopy and may reach heights of 200 feet. Leaves in the emergent layer are small and covered with a special wax to hold water. Seeds are blown to other parts of the forest. Trees that rise to the emergent layer are massive. Many are braced by huge buttress roots. Trunks can be 16 feet in circumference. Many animals that survive in the emergent layer never touch the ground.

questions.q: The Amazon rain forest covers an area nearly the size of the continent of Australia.
questions.explanation: True — the text says it covers nearly 2.8 million square miles, almost the size of Australia.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a layer of the rain forest?
questions.explanation: The four layers are forest floor, understory, canopy and emergent. Desert is not a rain-forest layer.

questions.q: Which layer of the rain forest is right above the forest floor?
questions.explanation: The passage describes the understory as the layer directly above the forest floor; the canopy and emergent sit higher.

questions.q: Most of the fruits and flowers of the rain forest grow in its...
questions.explanation: The canopy is 'where the wealth of the rain forest's fruits and flowers grow'. The emergent layer has massive trees, and the other layers are too dark.

questions.q: Which layer provides drinking pools for animals and breeding locations for tree frogs?
questions.explanation: Bromeliads in the canopy hold water for animals and tree frogs. The emergent layer is known for buttress roots, and the floor and understory for other features.

questions.q: Many trees in the ______ of the rain forest are braced by huge buttress roots.
questions.explanation: Emergent-layer trees are massive, braced by huge buttress roots, with trunks up to 16 feet around.

questions.q: Animals that live in the ______ may never touch the ground.
questions.explanation: The text states that many animals surviving in the emergent layer never touch the ground.

questions.q: Why do few plants grow in the understory?
questions.explanation: Only about 2–5% of sunlight reaches the understory, which limits growth. Water and nutrients are plentiful, and large leaves are an adaptation, not the cause.

questions.q: Why do plants in the understory have to rely on insects to pollinate them?
options: The sun is too bright in the understory.
The wind is too strong and seeds blow into the Amazon River.
There is very little wind in the understory.
There are very few butterflies in the rain forest.
questions.explanation: The understory is so thick that there is very little air movement, so plants depend on insects and animals for pollination.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT true?
options: The canopy is higher than the emergent layer.
The understory is below the canopy.
The Amazon rain forest is located in South America.
Leaves in the canopy are very dense and filter a high percentage of sunlight.
questions.explanation: The emergent layer is above the canopy, so claiming the canopy is higher is false. The other three statements are all true.

passages.title: The Beautiful, Powerful Jaguar
passages.text:
What beautiful cat lives in North and South America and is bigger and tougher than a leopard or mountain lion? If you said jaguar, you're right. The only cat species that are larger are the tiger, the African lion, and the endangered Asiatic lion.

Most jaguars are orange or tan with black rose-shaped spots (rosettes). However, there is also a solid black jaguar. Black jaguars have spots, too, but their spots are hard to see except when in bright sunlight.

The jaguar's coloration serves as camouflage. Lighter colored jaguars live in more open grassland and forest. Here, their markings help them blend among the vegetation and shadows. Black jaguars, meanwhile, blend in better in the darkest forests and jungles.

Like tigers, jaguars live alone most of their lives. Baby jaguars are born in litters of one to four and stay with their very protective mother, who guards and defends her young for two years while they learn to hunt. Then they leave to establish their own territories, marking it with their waste or by clawing marks in trees.

Also like tigers, jaguars love water. They will sit half-submerged, half-sinking in a cool rainforest stream or pond waiting for prey. Sometimes jaguars will even climb trees to await unsuspecting prey wandering below.

They'll catch water animals like caiman (a relative of alligators and crocodiles), fish, frogs and turtles. Other times, they'll hunt on land. They'll pounce on tapir, peccaries, capybara or deer with one quick leap. A jaguar's bite is so strong; it can even chomp through tortoise shells. They've even been observed using their jaws to drag heavy prey for over a mile.

People often confuse leopards with jaguars. Both are beautiful, spotted cats. However, there are several important differences. Leopards live in Asia and Africa, while jaguars are native to the Americas. Also, jaguars are much bigger. They have heavier chests and legs, and their larger heads have more powerful jaws.

While Jaguars were once fairly abundant and plentiful, they are now endangered and very few. Mining, farming and other development have destroyed much of their wild habitat. Today some of their habitat is protected. However, these beautiful cats are still illegally hunted for their fur and because they are a threat to ranchers' livestock.

questions.q: The 'endangered Asiatic lion'. Endangered means:
questions.explanation: Endangered means at risk of dying out. 'In great quantity' is the opposite, and 'dangerous' confuses it with the word 'danger'.

questions.q: Jaguars and leopards are alike because
questions.explanation: Both are large cats and both are spotted, so a and b are correct. Only jaguars live in the Americas — leopards live in Asia and Africa.

questions.q: Which cat species is smaller than a jaguar?
questions.explanation: The passage says jaguars are bigger than leopards or mountain lions. The tiger and both lions are listed as larger than jaguars.

questions.q: A camouflage helps an animal to
questions.explanation: Camouflage lets an animal blend into its surroundings, as jaguar markings do among vegetation and shadows.

questions.q: Baby jaguars stay with their mothers for ______ before going off on their own.
questions.explanation: The mother guards and defends her cubs for two years while they learn to hunt.

questions.q: Jaguars and leopards are different because
options: jaguars live in North and South America.
leopards live in Africa and Asia.
jaguars have heavier chests, legs, and heads.
questions.explanation: All three differences are stated: the two continents they live on, and the jaguar's heavier chest, legs and larger head with more powerful jaws.

questions.q: All the following statements are true EXCEPT
options: Jaguars can sometimes be found in streams or ponds.
Jaguars live in large groups throughout most of their lives.
questions.explanation: Jaguars live alone most of their lives, so this is false. They do climb trees and do sit half-submerged in streams and ponds.

passages.title: Mother and Child Relationships
passages.text:
It is important for a child to have a strong and positive relationship with his/her mother. The mother, or carer, should always be available and supportive of her child. Psychologists call this relationship 'secure attachment'.

However, sometimes a child does not have a secure attachment with the mother. The reasons for this include long-term illness or death of the mother. Other possible reasons are a long hospital stay for the child. When this happens, children sometimes grow up with various problems.

According to psychologists, these problems can be divided into four groups. The first group is emotional problems which affect the child's behaviour. An insecure attached child doesn't have much confidence and finds it difficult to deal with stress and other problems. The second group is physical; for example, the child may have a lot of illness or problems with eating food. In the third group, children often have many different types of social problems and have difficulty in making friends. They also sometimes have poor relationships with people. In a small number of cases, these children are violent and rebellious and their self-control is not very good so they become angry or upset very easily. They are not considerate to other people and they have a negative view of themselves. The final group of problems is connected with learning. Children without secure attachment have behaviour problems at school because they cannot control themselves. Some children talk too much in the lesson and ask too many questions. They may have speech and language problems and they may have difficulty in learning.

However, recent studies show that it is never too late to help children with their problems. New experiences can change connections in the brain. A child's relationships with relatives, teachers and other supportive adults can help him/her deal with his/her problems.

questions.q: What do psychologists call a strong and positive mother-child relationship?
questions.explanation: Psychologists use 'secure attachment' for a relationship where the mother or carer is always available and supportive. Insecure attachment is the opposite.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a reason for insecure attachment?
options: A long hospital stay for the child
questions.explanation: Financial difficulties are never mentioned. The passage lists the mother's illness or death and a long hospital stay for the child.

questions.q: How many groups of problems do psychologists divide insecure attachment into?
questions.explanation: Four — emotional, physical, social and learning problems are each described in turn.

questions.q: According to the passage, it is never too late to help children with their problems.
questions.explanation: True — recent studies show new experiences can change connections in the brain, so help is always possible.

questions.q: A child with insecure attachment may:
options: Have trouble making friends and controlling themselves
questions.explanation: The passage lists social problems (difficulty making friends) and poor self-control. Such children have behaviour problems at school and do have emotional problems.

passages.title: The Carbon Cycle
passages.text:
Today, I'm going to talk about one of the natural cycles on Earth. It is called the carbon cycle.

Firstly, where is carbon stored on Earth? The Earth's carbon is stored in four places. Most of the carbon is dissolved in the oceans, but some of it is in the atmosphere, some is in fossil fuels deep underground, and the rest is in the bodies of living things.

There are also four main production processes for carbon. Carbon is released into the atmosphere by animals and plants. This process is called respiration. Carbon dioxide is given out and oxygen is taken in.

Carbon dioxide is also released into the atmosphere during decomposition. This is the process of breaking down dead animals and plants. Animals and plants die, and bacteria decompose them. Carbon dioxide is released into the atmosphere and carbon is absorbed into the ground.

Thirdly, carbon dioxide is released during combustion. Combustion is also called burning.

Finally, carbon dioxide is released into the atmosphere by a process called outgassing. This happens when gas escapes from a volcano, for example.

There are two main consumption processes for carbon dioxide in the atmosphere. The first process is called photosynthesis. In this process, sunlight shines on the leaves of a plant, and the plant uses the light energy. It converts it into sugar and oxygen. During the process, carbon dioxide is consumed from the atmosphere.

Carbon dioxide is also dissolved in the oceans in a process called absorption. Carbon dioxide is absorbed at the surface and carried down to the deep ocean.

questions.q: Where is most of the carbon on Earth stored?
questions.explanation: Most carbon is dissolved in the oceans. Smaller amounts are in the atmosphere, fossil fuels and living things.

questions.q: What is the process called when animals and plants release CO2 into the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Respiration releases CO2 and takes in oxygen. Photosynthesis does the opposite, and decomposition and absorption are different processes.

questions.q: What is 'outgassing'?
questions.explanation: Outgassing is gas escaping, for example from a volcano. Burning is combustion and breaking down dead organisms is decomposition.

questions.q: Which process converts sunlight into sugar and oxygen?
questions.explanation: In photosynthesis the plant uses light energy to make sugar and oxygen while consuming CO2. Respiration and combustion release CO2 instead.

questions.q: What is combustion another word for?
questions.explanation: The passage states directly that combustion is also called burning.

questions.q: The main goal of education according to Unit 1 is to:
options: Facilitate learning and acquire knowledge through systematic teaching
questions.explanation: Education means acquiring knowledge, skills and values through teaching and learning. Memorizing facts is only one narrow method, and technology supports rather than replaces teaching.

questions.q: What is the 'flipped classroom' approach?
options: Teachers lecture during class and students do homework at home
Students watch videos at home and do practice in class with teacher guidance
Students teach the class instead of teachers
questions.explanation: In the flipped model, material is studied at home and class time is used for guided practice. Lecturing in class with homework at home is the traditional model.

questions.q: The present perfect continuous is used to:
options: Talk about recent, continuing actions or how long something has been happening
questions.explanation: It covers actions still continuing or their duration. Completed actions take the present perfect simple, future plans take 'going to', and past habits take 'used to'.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'I ______ chocolate since I was born.'
questions.explanation: 'Since' plus a starting point needs the present perfect simple: have liked. 'Has liked' cannot go with 'I', and the past or present simple break the time link.

questions.q: What does the word 'illiterate' mean?
questions.explanation: Illiterate means unable to read or write. Unable to speak is 'mute', unable to walk is 'immobile', and unable to see is 'blind'.

questions.q: A mentor is:
options: An experienced and trusted advisor or guide
questions.explanation: A mentor is an experienced, trusted guide. A struggling student is a mentee, and the other options are not people at all.

questions.q: In the context of education, 'digital literacy' refers to:
options: The ability to read and write
The ability to use digital technology and online resources effectively
The ability to program in Python
questions.explanation: Digital literacy is using digital technology and online resources effectively. Basic reading and writing is simple literacy, while repairing computers or coding is far narrower.

questions.q: What is 'problem-solving'?
options: The process of finding solutions to difficult or complex issues
questions.explanation: Problem-solving is finding solutions to difficult or complex issues. Creating or ignoring problems is the opposite, and memorized answers may not fit a new problem.

questions.q: Choose the correct form: 'She decided ______ two miles every day.'
questions.explanation: 'Decide' is followed by the to-infinitive: decided to run. Gerunds, bare infinitives and finite verbs do not follow 'decided'.

questions.q: What is the meaning of 'obsolete'?
options: No longer in use or outdated
questions.explanation: Obsolete means no longer in use or outdated. 'Very modern' is the opposite, and usefulness and price are unrelated to the meaning.

questions.q: Networking is:
options: The practice of making professional connections and relationships
questions.explanation: In this unit networking means building professional contacts. Connecting computers is the technical/IT meaning of the same word.

questions.q: What does 'rapport' mean?
options: A close and harmonious relationship or connection
questions.explanation: Rapport is a close, harmonious relationship. 'Report' is a similar-sounding word, and a meeting or business card is not a relationship.

questions.q: In networking, what should you do when you enter a room?
options: Wait for people to come to you
Approach groups of three people that contain at least one woman
questions.explanation: The unit's tip is to approach groups of three containing at least one woman. Waiting passively, avoiding eye contact or standing alone all block connections.

questions.q: What is the past perfect tense used for?
options: An event that occurred before another event in the past
questions.explanation: Past perfect marks an event that happened before another past event. Actions happening now take the present continuous, and routines take the present simple.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'We were late for the plane because we ______ our passports.'
questions.explanation: Forgetting happened before being late, so the past perfect 'had forgotten' is needed. 'Forgot' would lose the sequence, and the other forms do not fit the past narrative.

questions.q: What does 'collaboration' mean?
options: The act of working together or cooperating with others
questions.explanation: Collaboration is working together or cooperating. Working alone, competing and ignoring others are all the opposite of it.

questions.q: A 'seminar' is:
options: A conference or meeting for discussion and learning
questions.explanation: A seminar is a meeting for discussion and learning. An exam assesses knowledge rather than discussing it, and the other options are unrelated.

questions.q: What is 'body language'?
options: Non-verbal communication through gestures, posture, and facial expressions
A language spoken in one country
questions.explanation: Body language is non-verbal communication through gestures, posture and facial expressions — so it is neither a spoken nor a written language.

questions.q: What does 'potential' mean?
options: Having the capability to develop or achieve something
questions.explanation: Potential means having the capability to develop or achieve something. 'Having no ability' is the opposite, and age and tiredness are unrelated.

questions.q: What is 'etiquette'?
options: The customary code of polite behavior in society
questions.explanation: Etiquette is the customary code of polite behaviour in society — not food, technology or a language.

questions.q: What does 'monochronic' refer to?
options: A cultural preference for doing one thing at a time and valuing punctuality
questions.explanation: Monochronic cultures do one thing at a time and value punctuality. Doing many things at once describes polychronic cultures.

questions.q: What does 'polychronic' refer to?
options: Doing one thing at a time
A cultural preference for doing multiple tasks at once and valuing flexibility
questions.explanation: Polychronic cultures handle several tasks at once and value flexibility. Doing one thing at a time is monochronic, and the other options are unrelated.

questions.q: A 'stereotype' is:
options: A widely held but oversimplified belief or idea about a particular type of person
questions.explanation: A stereotype is a widely held but oversimplified belief about a type of person. It is an unverified generalization, not a proven scientific fact.

questions.q: What does 'tolerance' mean?
options: The acceptance of different opinions, beliefs, or practices
questions.explanation: Tolerance is accepting different opinions, beliefs or practices. Refusing to accept differences is intolerance, the exact opposite.

questions.q: What is 'proxemics'?
options: The study of space in communication
questions.explanation: Proxemics studies how space and distance function in communication. Numbers belong to mathematics, ancient civilizations to archaeology, and weather to meteorology.

questions.q: What does 'assume' mean?
options: To take for granted without proof; suppose
questions.explanation: Assume means to take for granted without proof. Proving needs evidence, questioning rejects a claim, and denying is the opposite of assuming.

questions.q: What is an 'artefact'?
options: An object made by a human being, typically of historical or cultural significance
questions.explanation: An artefact is a human-made object of historical or cultural significance — so it is not a modern invention, a food or an animal.

questions.q: What does 'controversial' mean?
questions.explanation: Controversial means causing disagreement or dispute. If everyone agreed there would be no controversy, and age is irrelevant to the meaning.

questions.q: What is a 'researcher'?
options: A person who conducts investigations to gather information and knowledge
questions.explanation: A researcher conducts investigations to gather information and knowledge. Teaching, selling and driving are separate occupations.

questions.q: In the context of research, what does 'statistics' refer to?
options: The art of storytelling through data
The collection and analysis of numerical data
questions.explanation: Statistics is the collection and analysis of numerical data. The other options describe storytelling, biology and history, not statistics.

questions.q: In the future, robots might be used in ______ labor, or to perform other hazardous tasks.
questions.explanation: Manual labour is physical work done by hand. 'Delicate' describes fragility, and 'initiative' and 'reliable' are not types of labour.

questions.q: The following has the same meaning as the word 'GLOBAL'.
questions.explanation: Global means worldwide, which matches 'universal'. The other three all mean limited or narrow in scope, the opposite of global.

questions.q: ______ is someone who provides guidance to learners telling them how to do something.
questions.explanation: A tutor guides learners. A pilot flies aircraft, an actor performs, and a pirate robs ships — none of these teach.

questions.q: The president's family was a humble ______; they were poor people without a good position in society.
questions.explanation: 'Origins' refers to a person's family background. Cultures, dimensions and nationalities do not fit 'humble' or the idea of low social position.

questions.q: In the context of including or containing, what is a synonym for the word 'comprise'?
questions.explanation: Comprise means to include or contain, so 'encompass' is the synonym. Exclude and remove are opposites, and divide means to separate.

questions.q: Our professor ______ a lot of research on stem cells.
questions.explanation: 'Do research' is the correct collocation. You do not 'make', 'win' or 'achieve' research.

questions.q: What is the opposite of the word 'polychronic'?
questions.explanation: Monochronic (one task at a time) is the direct opposite of polychronic (many tasks at once). The other options are not antonyms.

questions.q: She is ______; she has a PhD in neuroscience.
questions.explanation: 'Well-educated' is the correct compound adjective. The other forms are misspelled or grammatically impossible in English.

questions.q: The project was completed on time due to the team's ______.
questions.explanation: Dedication means commitment and hard work, which explains finishing on time. Humour, 'effortless efforts' and charity do not cause timely completion.

questions.q: An unfair and unreasonable opinion or feeling, especially when formed without enough thought or knowledge.
questions.explanation: Prejudice is a preconceived, unfair opinion formed without knowledge. Karma, justice and fairness all imply balance or fairness, the opposite idea.

questions.q: ______ has become a powerful asset in the current workplace.
questions.explanation: Emotional intelligence is highly valued in modern workplaces. 'Currying favor' is flattery, and 'unoriginally' is an adverb, so neither fits.

questions.q: It's a cheap ring but it has a great sentimental ______ for me.
questions.explanation: 'Sentimental value' is the fixed phrase for emotional worth. Tradition, belief and fashion do not collocate with 'sentimental'.

questions.q: Includes transportation systems, communication networks, sewage, water and school systems.
questions.explanation: Infrastructure refers to the fundamental systems a society needs. Overpopulation, overcrowding and biodiversity describe population and nature, not built systems.

questions.q: What does the term 'millennial' refer to?
options: A type of ancient writing system
A type of renewable energy source
A person belonging to the generation between the 1980s and 2000s
questions.explanation: A millennial is someone born roughly between the early 1980s and late 1990s. The other options are unrelated to the term.

questions.q: The city flourished in the post-war period, witnessed rapid growth and revitalization. The prefix 'post' means:
questions.explanation: The prefix 'post-' means after, so 'post-war' = after the war. 'Pre-' would mean before, and 'since' or 'during' are not prefixes here.

questions.q: Can I connect to your ______ please? I don't have enough data on my phone.
questions.explanation: A mobile hotspot shares your phone's internet connection. A cookie and browser are software, and a power bank only charges battery.

questions.q: The factory's old machines were causing pollution and were ______, so they had to be replaced.
questions.explanation: Unsustainable means impossible to maintain without harm, which fits the pollution context. 'Insustainable' and 'dissustainable' are not real words, and 'sustainable' is the opposite.

questions.q: Archaeologists study artifacts and fossils to uncover the mysteries of human life in PREHISTORY.
options: The detailed records of a medieval kingdom
questions.explanation: Prehistory is the period before written records, which is why archaeologists study objects and fossils rather than documents. All other options describe documented historical periods.

questions.q: The painting in the museum is ______ but there are hundreds of copies.
questions.explanation: 'Original' means the authentic first version, contrasted with copies. Global, cultural and critical do not express authenticity.

questions.q: You need to plan ahead to ______ your goals.
questions.explanation: 'Achieve goals' is the correct collocation. 'Do', 'study' and 'become' do not collocate with 'goals'.

questions.q: Digital literacy is becoming ______ these days.
questions.explanation: Digital literacy is becoming increasingly popular/important. 'Obsolete' is the opposite, and 'fashionable' and 'interesting' do not fit the meaning of a growing skill.

questions.q: An operation is beginning to try to save species of crocodile from ______.
questions.explanation: Extinction means the complete disappearance of a species, which is what the operation is trying to prevent. The other options are unrelated.

questions.q: I can't ______ accessing this website! My laptop might get hacked.
questions.explanation: 'Risk accessing' means to take the chance of accessing. 'Link' and 'log' are not followed by 'accessing', and 'access accessing' is redundant.

questions.q: I can't think of a better ______ for the job.
questions.explanation: A candidate is a person suited to a job. An offer, boss or competition are not people who fill the position.

questions.q: Choose the appropriate prefix to the word 'do'.
questions.explanation: 'Undo' means to reverse an action. 'Non-', 'im-' and 'dis-' do not combine with 'do' to form that meaning.

questions.q: Have you ever been to ______ Paris?
questions.explanation: No article is used before city names like Paris. Articles 'the', 'a' and 'an' are not used with singular city names.

questions.q: I like reading ______ short stories.
questions.explanation: No article is used with plural nouns spoken about in general. 'The' would refer to specific stories and 'a'/'an' cannot go with plurals.

questions.q: What is the meaning of 'outstanding'?
questions.explanation: Outstanding means exceptionally good, so 'excellent'. 'Expensive', 'energetic' and 'expected' do not carry that meaning.

questions.q: Scientists ______ any possibility that the earth is flat.
questions.explanation: Scientists disprove the flat-earth idea, i.e. show it is false. 'Prove' would mean the opposite, and 'dysfunction' is not a verb.

questions.q: Governments should depend on ______ to get reliable researches.
questions.explanation: Research organizations are the bodies that conduct reliable studies. Journals publish findings and a foundation funds work, but neither does the research.

questions.q: USA is known for its cultural ______.
questions.explanation: 'Cultural diversity' is the standard phrase. 'Flexibility' and 'amount' do not collocate with 'cultural' in this sense.

questions.q: We challenged his political ______.
questions.explanation: 'Beliefs' is the correct plural noun. 'Believes' is a verb form and 'talks' does not collocate with 'political' here.

questions.q: I cannot ______.
questions.explanation: 'Get the point' means to understand. The other phrasal verbs need objects ('get along with someone', 'get through something') to be complete.

questions.q: Customs officers must ______ our passport before travelling.
questions.explanation: Validate means to officially check and confirm. 'Allow' means permit, which is not what officers do to a passport.

questions.q: The weather looked bad but they insisted on continuing their picnic ______.
questions.explanation: 'Regardless' means without being affected by the weather. 'Definitely' and 'absolutely' express certainty, not disregard of a condition.

questions.q: His boss ______ him for his bad work habits.
questions.explanation: Criticized means expressed disapproval, which fits bad work habits. 'Praised' is the opposite, and 'pretend' is a base verb that cannot take '-ed'.

questions.q: He ______ photos from his digital camera to his computer.
questions.explanation: Uploaded means transferred files to a computer or network. 'Signed' and 'saved' do not describe that transfer.

questions.q: The company has a plan to ______ a new product.
questions.explanation: 'Launch a new product' means to introduce it to the market. 'Cancel' is the opposite, and 'buy' does not collocate with launching.

questions.q: He showed ______ against women in particular.
questions.explanation: Bias means prejudice against a group. 'Tendency' is neutral, and 'admiration' is a positive feeling, not hostility.

questions.q: Changing one's mind many times about a specific decision shows ______ and hesitation.
questions.explanation: Uncertainty means not being sure, which matches repeated changes of mind. 'Corruption' is dishonesty and 'comfort' is unrelated.

questions.q: The word ______ refers to a group of people living in the same place or having a particular characteristic in common.
questions.explanation: Community is the correct term for such a group. A 'circle' is a social group and a 'band' is a small music group — neither fits the definition.

questions.q: Before writing your essay, please read the question ______ carefully.
questions.explanation: A prompt is the question or instruction you respond to. 'Promotion' and 'response' do not match this meaning.

questions.q: One type of learners is the ______ learner who needs to view material in order to effectively learn.
questions.explanation: Visual learners learn best by seeing. 'Recurrent' and 'reluctant' describe frequency or willingness, not a learning style.

questions.q: The ______ idea of your project is good but it needs further details.
questions.explanation: 'Initial' means the first or beginning idea. 'Formal' and 'repeated' do not fit the idea of a starting concept.

questions.q: The report has so many mistakes. The operations department will take the ______ for drafting such a report.
questions.explanation: 'Take the blame' means accept responsibility. 'Take the act' and 'take the refuse' are not English expressions.

questions.q: A tutor should ______ students to pose questions in class.
questions.explanation: Encourage means to support or motivate. 'Response' is a noun, and 'progress' does not mean to motivate someone.

questions.q: A child needs to ______ with the surrounding objects.
questions.explanation: 'Experiment with' means to try things out, which fits exploring objects. 'Cover' and 'recognize' do not take 'with' in this sense.

questions.q: I was absent last lecture and my ______ says that the lecturer needs a draft of the research paper by next week.
questions.explanation: A classmate would be the one to inform you about lecture instructions. A janitor and a manager are not in your class.

questions.q: The third type of memory is the ______ memory that has to do with our senses.
questions.explanation: Sensory memory relates to information from the senses. 'Fragile' and 'short-term' do not describe sensory input.

questions.q: The presenter has successfully ______ all audience.
questions.explanation: Involved means engaged the audience, which presenters aim for. 'Invaded' is hostile and 'performed' does not take 'audience' as object here.

questions.q: The report ______ section informs that the project has to reach a closer within the next 6 months.
questions.explanation: The 'findings' section reports results. 'Found' is a verb and 'employees' is not a report section.

questions.q: A ______ plan gives a clue to the consequences that are going to happen in the near future.
questions.explanation: A short-term plan concerns the near future. 'Long-term' is the opposite, and 'moderate-term' is not a standard term.

questions.q: I don't know the name of the man, but I can surely ______ his face.
questions.explanation: Recognize means to identify someone. 'Refill' and 'redeem' have unrelated meanings.

questions.q: This project's budget will ______ be 10,000,000 $.
questions.explanation: Approximately means about or roughly. 'Average' and 'difficult' do not modify a figure as an adverb.

questions.q: The word 'major' is a ______ for the word 'important'.
questions.explanation: Synonym means a word with the same meaning. An antonym means the opposite, and an acronym is an abbreviation.

questions.q: I need to hire an ______ secretary with five years experience.
questions.explanation: Efficient means productive, which is the quality sought. 'Affect' is a verb and 'affective' relates to emotions.

questions.q: The ______ decided to operate on the infected leg tomorrow morning.
questions.explanation: A surgeon performs operations. A clown and a professor are not medical roles.

questions.q: After your accident, I decided to put ______ cycling.
questions.explanation: 'Put off' means postpone or stop doing something. 'Put out' means extinguish and 'put on' means wear or gain weight.

questions.q: For many cultures, the handshake is a sign of ______.
questions.explanation: A handshake is a greeting. 'Fleeting' means brief and 'grieving' means mourning — neither matches.

questions.q: Arranging ______ means arranging a place to stay.
questions.explanation: Accommodations means lodging or a place to stay. 'Accounting' and 'acclamations' have completely different meanings.

questions.q: Competitors usually compete on the ______.
questions.explanation: An ice rink is the surface where skating competitions take place. 'Iceberg' is floating ice and 'ice ring' is not a real term.

questions.q: Let's ______ the situation.
questions.explanation: 'Make the most of' means to use a situation well. 'Make up' means invent or reconcile, and 'make good' means succeed.

questions.q: To look at the differences between two or more things is to ______.
questions.explanation: Compare means to examine similarities and differences. 'Ruin' means destroy and 'startle' means surprise.

questions.q: I'm ______ to go.
questions.explanation: 'All ready' means fully prepared. 'Already' means by now, and 'readily' means willingly.

questions.q: My bookcase is a mess. I need to ______ my books.
questions.explanation: 'Sort out' means organize. 'Put up' means erect or accommodate, and 'fix up' means repair or arrange.

questions.q: He finally ______ his mind and decided to retire early.
questions.explanation: 'Made up his mind' means decided. 'Ran into' means met by chance and 'bought into' means accepted an idea.

questions.q: 'The band is going to play live later today.' Find the antonym for the word 'live'.
questions.explanation: 'Recorded' is the opposite of a live performance. 'Alive' means living and 'great' means excellent.

questions.q: Helping animals is what ______. He just can't stand it.
questions.explanation: 'Makes him tick' means motivates or drives him. The other options are either not idioms or grammatically wrong.

questions.q: The workers stayed on the job till ______.
questions.explanation: 'Till daylight' means until morning light. 'Daydream' is a mental state and 'daybreak' refers to the moment dawn begins.

questions.q: That is an ______ different problem.
questions.explanation: 'Altogether' means completely. 'All together' means everyone in one place, and 'ill together' is not a phrase.

questions.q: I can ______ the shopping tonight.
questions.explanation: 'Do the shopping' is the correct collocation. 'Make' and 'go' do not take 'the shopping' as an object.

questions.q: A small booklet with pictures and information about a product is called a ______.
questions.explanation: A brochure is a small informational booklet. A novel is fiction and an autobiography is a life story — neither advertises products.

questions.q: I forgot to ______ you to my friend Jennifer.
questions.explanation: 'Introduce someone to someone' is the correct phrase. 'Inform' means tell and 'bring' means carry along.

questions.q: Guess who I ______ yesterday?
questions.explanation: 'Ran into' means met by chance. 'Made up' means invented or reconciled, and 'put on' means wore or gained.

questions.q: George can't stand his work anymore. If I were in his shoes I would ______ that lousy job.
questions.explanation: Quit means to leave a job. 'Quiz' and 'quote' are unrelated in meaning.

questions.q: I like seafood especially ______.
questions.explanation: Shrimps are seafood. Seals are mammals and jellyfish, while technically edible in some cultures, are not the standard seafood answer here.

questions.q: Let's ______ skiing.
questions.explanation: 'Go skiing' is the correct collocation with -ing sports. 'Play' and 'do' are not used with skiing.

questions.q: A carpenter ______.
questions.explanation: A carpenter builds and repairs wooden structures, including homes. Cleaning and demolishing are other trades.

questions.q: Her ______ in music showed at an early age.
questions.explanation: 'Talent in' is the correct collocation. 'Ability in' is less standard, and 'distaste' is a negative feeling.

questions.q: In which word are the letters 'gh' silent?
questions.explanation: In 'neighbor' the 'gh' is silent. In 'rough' and 'enough' the 'gh' is pronounced as /f/.

questions.q: In which word is the letter 'g' silent?
questions.explanation: In 'sign' the 'g' is silent. 'Lgnore' is a misspelling of 'ignore' (where g is pronounced), and in 'finger' the g is pronounced.

questions.q: He has 'a great deal' of patience. What does 'a great deal' mean?
questions.explanation: 'A great deal' means a lot of. 'Very little' is the opposite, and 'most' expresses a comparative, not a large quantity.

questions.q: Mountain climbing is a ______ sport.
questions.explanation: 'Dangerous' is the adjective modifying 'sport'. 'Dangerously' is an adverb and 'dangerly' is not a word.

questions.q: This cake is delicious! What are the ______?
questions.explanation: Ingredients are what a cake is made of. A recipe is the instruction, a flavour is a taste, and a material is for building.

questions.q: This medicine is very ______ tasting.
questions.explanation: Bitter is a taste, so it describes the medicine. 'Worse' and 'worst' are comparisons and 'annoying' describes annoyance.

questions.q: We took the children for ice cream at a shop that has over 30 different ______.
questions.explanation: Ice cream comes in flavours. 'Kinds' is too general and does not fit the ice-cream context as well.

questions.q: She made a ______ drink using a banana, milk, and frozen blueberries.
questions.explanation: A 'smooth drink' describes its texture, which matches a blended fruit drink. 'Delicious' and 'great' are opinions, and 'delicate' means fragile.

questions.q: The tea was very hot so she had to ______ it very slowly.
questions.explanation: 'Sip' means to drink slowly, which fits very hot tea. 'Drinking' and 'sipping' are -ing forms, and 'drink' does not convey slowness.

questions.q: What is 'rote learning'?
questions.explanation: Rote learning is memorization by repetition, without understanding. The other options describe deep, practical or peer-based learning.

questions.q: What does 'retrieve' mean in the context of memory?
options: To bring back information from memory
questions.explanation: Retrieve means to bring stored information back into mind. Forgetting is the opposite, and storing and encoding are earlier memory stages.

questions.q: What did Mace call the technique of revising at intervals (10 min, 1 day, 1 week)?
questions.explanation: Mace named it 'spaced repetition' — reviewing at increasing intervals. Massed practice, rote learning and cramming all mean the opposite.

questions.q: According to research, what percentage of learners are multi-mode?
questions.explanation: Research shows 60-70% of learners use more than one mode. The other figures are too low or too high.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the learning styles mentioned in the workbook?
questions.explanation: 'Pessimistic' is a personality trait, not a learning style. Visual, aural and kinaesthetic are all listed learning styles.

questions.q: According to Milliken (1981), the three barriers to friendship are:
questions.explanation: Milliken identified acceptance, approval and appreciation as the three barriers. The other groups are not the model Milliken proposed.

questions.q: What is the difference between an acquaintance and a friend?
options: An acquaintance is someone you know; a friend is someone you like
An acquaintance is family; a friend is a stranger
An acquaintance is older than a friend
questions.explanation: Per the workbook, an acquaintance is someone you know; a friend is someone you like. The other options misstate the relationship.

questions.q: Which phrase means 'taking responsibility' in an apology?
questions.explanation: 'It's my fault' explicitly accepts responsibility. A general apology, an excuse and an offer to replace something do not.

questions.q: What does 'laissez-faire' management mean?
options: Managers give orders and expect obedience
Managers give staff complete freedom without interfering
Managers delegate only to senior staff
questions.explanation: Laissez-faire means 'leave alone', so managers give complete freedom. The other options describe authoritarian or selective delegation styles.

questions.q: Who wrote 'The Inner Game of Tennis' in 1974?
questions.explanation: Gallway wrote 'The Inner Game of Tennis' in 1974. Milliken, Berne and Boas wrote about different topics.

questions.q: According to Gallway, Self 1 is ______ and Self 2 is ______.
questions.explanation: Self 1 is confident (how others see us) and Self 2 is doubtful (how we see ourselves). The other pairs reverse or misrepresent Gallway's model.

questions.q: Which is the largest desert in the world?
questions.explanation: The Sahara is the largest hot desert. The Gobi, Kalahari and Mojave are all much smaller.

questions.q: What is desertification?
options: The process of fertile land turning into desert
questions.explanation: Desertification is fertile land becoming desert. The other options describe unrelated activities, none of which is land degradation.

questions.q: What is a 'biome'?
options: A major environment covering a large area of Earth
questions.explanation: A biome is a large-scale environment type (e.g. rain forest, tundra). A single species or small habitat is far narrower.

questions.q: Franz Boas was a famous:
questions.explanation: Boas was a pioneering anthropologist. While he studied language, his primary field was anthropology.

questions.q: Franz Boas emigrated to the US in:
questions.explanation: Boas emigrated to the US in 1885. The other dates do not match his biography.

questions.q: What did Franz Boas believe about Western civilization?
options: It is the standard for other cultures
It is not the standard for other cultures
It is superior to all others
questions.explanation: Boas argued Western civilization is NOT the standard for judging other cultures. The other options reflect the ethnocentric view he opposed.

questions.q: What is a poltergeist?
options: A mythical creature that throws things around
An evil spirit that haunts churches
questions.explanation: A poltergeist is a mythical creature that throws objects. It is not a tradition, a building or a church spirit.

questions.q: In Germany, why do guests throw old cups and plates before a wedding?
options: To make noise for the neighbours
questions.explanation: The custom started to frighten poltergeists away with loud noise. Good luck and celebration came to be associated with it, but the original reason was the poltergeist.

questions.q: Which is the formal verb for 'cut down'?
questions.explanation: Reduce is the formal verb for 'cut down'. The other options have entirely different meanings.

questions.q: Which is the formal verb for 'go to'?
questions.explanation: Attend is the formal equivalent of 'go to' (e.g. attend a meeting). The other options do not mean 'go to'.

questions.q: Which is the informal verb for 'select'?
questions.explanation: Choose is the informal verb for select. Attend, reduce and ensure have unrelated meanings.

questions.q: Which is the formal verb for 'want'?
questions.explanation: Intend is the formal verb closest to 'want' (in the sense of planning). The other options do not carry that meaning.

questions.q: Which is the formal verb for 'call'?
questions.explanation: Name is the formal verb for 'call' (e.g. 'they named him chairman'). The other options have unrelated meanings.

questions.q: Which is the formal verb for 'think about'?
questions.explanation: Consider is the formal verb for 'think about'. The other options have unrelated meanings.

questions.q: In 2014, the highest percentage of obese children lived in:
questions.explanation: Nearly half of obese children under five in 2014 lived in Asia. The other regions had lower proportions.

questions.q: What is the primary treatment for obesity?
questions.explanation: Diet and exercise are the primary treatments. Surgery and drugs are used in specific severe cases, and psychiatric therapy is not the main treatment.

questions.q: How many eggs does a female Emperor Penguin lay?
questions.explanation: The female Emperor Penguin lays one egg. Any higher number is incorrect for this species.

questions.q: Which animal only preys on Penguin chicks?
questions.explanation: Skuas prey on penguin chicks. Seals, sharks and orcas also prey on penguins but take adults as well.

questions.q: How do warblers navigate during daylight?
options: They rely on the sun for guidance
questions.explanation: Warblers use the sun for guidance in daylight. Stars are used at night, so the other daytime options are wrong.

questions.q: Why are owls effective nocturnal hunters?
options: They have great night vision and excellent hearing
They have a strong sense of smell
questions.explanation: Owls rely on keen night vision and hearing. Their sense of smell, speed and size are not their main hunting advantages.

questions.q: What are the three components of the habit loop?
questions.explanation: The habit loop is cue, routine, reward. The other groups use different terms and do not describe the standard model.

questions.q: What was the first video uploaded to YouTube?
questions.explanation: 'Me at the zoo' was the first YouTube video. The other options are categories of later content.

questions.q: Where was Madame Tussauds' first permanent exhibition located?
questions.explanation: The first permanent exhibition was on Baker Street in London. The other cities host later branches.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'I know you will not believe it. I hate ______ video games very much.'
questions.explanation: 'Hate' is followed by a gerund: hate playing. The other forms do not follow 'hate'.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'He will be in his office in ______ hour.'
questions.explanation: 'An' is used before a vowel sound; 'hour' begins with a vowel sound because the 'h' is silent. 'A' would be wrong before a vowel sound.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'You are not allowed ______ class without taking permission.'
questions.explanation: 'Allowed' is followed by the to-infinitive: allowed to leave. The other forms do not follow 'allowed'.

questions.q: Which prefix is used to indicate too much of something?
questions.explanation: 'Over-' means too much (e.g. overdramatic). 'Un-' means not, 're-' means again, and 'under-' means too little.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'In 2025, my brother ______ international law at the university.'
questions.explanation: A future time reference needs the future continuous: will be studying. The other forms are present or non-finite.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'The food here is awful, I don't think people in this restaurant ______ cook.'
questions.explanation: 'Can' expresses ability, which fits the idea that the cooks are unable to cook well. The other modals express obligation or prohibition.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'If you had worked hard, you ______ a raise.'
questions.explanation: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle. The other forms belong to the first or second conditional.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'If you buy her flowers, she ______ happy.'
questions.explanation: First conditional: if + present simple, will + infinitive. The other options are the second or third conditional forms.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'He forgot how ______ the microwave.'
questions.explanation: 'Forget how' takes the to-infinitive: forgot how to use. The other forms do not follow this structure.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'Our sales ______ over the past five years and are still going up.'
questions.explanation: 'Over the past five years' requires the present perfect: have increased. The other forms do not link the past to now.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'Somebody ______ my cookies. There are very few left.'
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous: has been eating (someone has been doing it up to now). 'Have' is wrong with 'somebody'.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'The candidate ______ a meeting with the CEO. Before that, he had met the manager.'
questions.explanation: Past perfect of 'have' is 'had had' — the meeting happened before the earlier meeting. The other forms do not show the past-before-past sequence.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'Prices ______ nowadays; it doesn't seem they will stop rising anytime soon.'
questions.explanation: 'Nowadays' with an ongoing action takes the present continuous: are soaring. The other forms do not fit the ongoing present.

questions.q: What is the active form of: 'Handball is played'?
questions.explanation: Passive 'is played' (present simple) converts to active 'They play handball'. The others change the tense or add a different aspect.

questions.q: What is the passive form of: 'Julia rescued three cats'?
options: Three cats are rescued by Julia
Three cats had been rescued by Julia
Three cats were rescued by Julia
questions.explanation: Past simple passive: was/were + past participle: were rescued. The other options change the tense or keep the sentence active.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'The project depends ______ the newly approved budget.'
questions.explanation: 'Depend' takes the preposition 'on'. The other prepositions do not collocate with 'depend'.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'Many accidents are caused ______ people driving too fast.'
questions.explanation: Passive voice uses 'by' for the agent: caused by. The other prepositions do not mark the agent.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: 'Ahmad said, "I am sorry"'
options: Ahmad said that I was sorry
Ahmad said that he is sorry
Ahmad said that he was sorry
Ahmad said that he had been sorry
questions.explanation: Present simple 'am' becomes past simple 'was'; 'I' becomes 'he'. The other options keep the wrong tense or the wrong pronoun.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: 'She said, "I have broken your pen"'
options: She told me that I had broken her pen
She told me that she had broken my pen
She told me that she has broken my pen
She told me that she broke your pen
questions.explanation: Present perfect becomes past perfect; 'your' becomes 'my'. The other options swap the pronouns or keep the wrong tense.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: 'Ali said, "I am studying now"'
options: Ali said that he was studying then
Ali said that he is studying now
Ali said that he was studying now
Ali said that he had been studying then
questions.explanation: Present continuous becomes past continuous; 'now' becomes 'then'. The other options keep the wrong tense or the wrong time word.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'She asked her colleague ______ offer some help.'
questions.explanation: 'Ask someone to do something' uses 'to' + infinitive. The other prepositions do not follow 'asked someone'.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'He is fed up ______ this meeting.'
questions.explanation: 'Fed up' takes 'with'. The other prepositions do not collocate with 'fed up'.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'She spends so much money and time ______ clothes and shopping.'
questions.explanation: 'Spend money/time on something' uses 'on'. The other prepositions do not collocate with 'spend'.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'I'm looking forward to ______ her soon.'
questions.explanation: 'Looking forward to' takes a gerund: meeting. The other forms do not follow the preposition 'to' here.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'She remembered how ______ an essay.'
questions.explanation: 'Remember how' takes the to-infinitive: how to write. The other forms do not follow this structure.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'This year we ______ new teaching methods.'
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous: have been using. 'Are been using' is ungrammatical, and 'is/has' do not agree with 'we'.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'She ______ drive her father's car when she was only 15.'
questions.explanation: Past passive: was allowed to. The other forms use the wrong tense or omit the auxiliary.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'Professor Fouad specializes ______ mechanical engineering.'
questions.explanation: 'Specialize' takes 'in'. The other prepositions do not collocate with 'specialize'.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'She requested this information ______ forwarded to her e-mail.'
questions.explanation: 'Request something to be + past participle' is the correct passive structure: to be forwarded. The other forms do not complete the structure.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'Does this dictionary belong ______ you?'
questions.explanation: 'Belong to' means be owned by. The other prepositions do not collocate with 'belong' in this meaning.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'I find it very difficult to concentrate ______ the presentation when I am hungry.'
questions.explanation: 'Concentrate' takes 'on'. The other prepositions do not collocate with 'concentrate'.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'You shouldn't be critical ______ others.'
questions.explanation: 'Critical of' means disapproving of. The other prepositions do not collocate with 'critical'.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'This book deals ______ the idea of National Independence.'
questions.explanation: 'Deal with' means to be about or handle. The other prepositions do not collocate with 'deal' in this sense.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'He suggested ______ to Spain for Christmas holidays.'
questions.explanation: 'Suggest' takes a gerund: suggested going. The other forms do not follow 'suggest'.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'She remembered ______ the book on the shelf.'
questions.explanation: 'Remember doing' means recall a past action: remembered putting. The other forms do not follow this structure.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'She provided us ______ the missing data.'
questions.explanation: 'Provide someone with something' uses 'with'. The other prepositions do not collocate with 'provide'.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'I am thinking ______ buying a new house.'
questions.explanation: 'Think of doing something' uses 'of' + gerund. The other prepositions do not collocate with 'think' in this sense.

questions.q: Please remind me ______ the dishes.
questions.explanation: 'Remind someone to do something' uses 'to' + base verb. 'To washes' is ungrammatical and 'washing' does not follow 'remind'.

questions.q: She agreed ______ us next week.
questions.explanation: 'Agree' takes the to-infinitive: agreed to visit. The other forms do not follow 'agree'.

questions.q: We ______ all the books we had yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' requires the past simple: sold. The other forms are present or non-finite.

questions.q: Websites that help students to find scholarships to study abroad ______.
questions.explanation: The main clause needs a verb: are not very reliable. The other options repeat the relative pronoun or add a redundant subject.

questions.q: The divorce rate in Sweden is ______ the rate in France.
questions.explanation: Comparative of equality: as + adjective + as. The other options omit one 'as'.

questions.q: Companies which ______ by young directors are a good example of successful business.
questions.explanation: Passive voice in a relative clause: which are led. 'Are leading' is active, and 'they are led' repeats the subject.

questions.q: If I ______ you, I would accept his offer.
questions.explanation: Second conditional uses 'were' for all subjects in the if-clause. 'Would be' and 'am' do not fit this structure.

questions.q: When one ignores a problem, it ______ worse.
questions.explanation: Zero conditional for a general truth: present simple 'gets'. 'Would get' is conditional and 'will get' suggests a specific future.

questions.q: Julius Caesar conquered the world. He was still betrayed. The best way to join the two sentences is:
options: He conquered the world, Julius Caesar who was still betrayed.
Julius Caesar, who conquered the world, was still betrayed.
Julius Caesar, who was still betrayed, he conquered the world.
questions.explanation: The non-defining relative clause 'who conquered the world' is set off by commas inside the main clause. The other options are ungrammatical or repeat the subject.

questions.q: How come ______ so early?
questions.explanation: 'How come' is followed by statement word order: subject + verb. The other options use question inversion, which is wrong here.

questions.q: Sarah travelled to Spain, ______ she studied engineering and got her master's degree.
questions.explanation: 'Where' refers to a place: Spain. 'Which' would refer to the whole clause and 'that' cannot follow a comma in a non-defining clause.

questions.q: To be able to fit in a new community, you should deal ______ all sorts of people.
questions.explanation: 'Deal with' means interact with or handle. The other prepositions do not collocate with 'deal' in this sense.

questions.q: Books that contain inappropriate content ______.
questions.explanation: Modal passive: must be + past participle. 'Must to be' is ungrammatical and 'they must be banned' repeats the subject.

questions.q: This issue ______ very infuriating.
questions.explanation: Correct word order is 'is also'. The other options misplace the adverb or omit the verb.

questions.q: Barack Obama, the president of the U.S., ______ stayed in office for two successful terms.
questions.explanation: The non-defining relative clause needs 'who was'. 'Who he was' repeats the subject and 'which' cannot refer to a person.

questions.q: You love her, ______ you?
questions.explanation: The question tag for 'you love' is 'don't you?'. 'Are' and 'do' do not match the auxiliary or polarity.

questions.q: I miss the old days, when I was just a child and I ______ stay with my grandparents all the time.
questions.explanation: 'Used to' + infinitive expresses a past habit. 'Used' alone is not enough and 'am used to' refers to a present habit.

questions.q: Ahmed: 'Could you help me with my research, Sara?' Sara: ______ Use 'Ask'
options: Ahmed asked me to help him with his research.
Ahmed promised to help Sara with her research.
Sara asked him to help her with the research.
questions.explanation: Reported request: Ahmed asked me to help him with his research. The other options reverse the roles or change the speech act.

questions.q: ______ brushing her teeth, she likes to read in bed before sleeping.
questions.explanation: 'After + gerund' shows sequence: after brushing. 'As' and 'when' suggest simultaneity, not sequence.

questions.q: The verb 'sleep' is an example of an ______ verb. It doesn't require an object.
questions.explanation: Intransitive verbs do not take a direct object. Transitive verbs do take an object, and 'reported' is not a verb type.

questions.q: The verb 'give' is an example of a ______ verb. It needs two objects.
questions.explanation: Transitive verbs take objects; 'give' takes two (give someone something). Intransitive verbs do not take objects, and 'transformative' is not a grammar term.

questions.q: I think ______ you can emphasize an apology by saying really or very.
questions.explanation: 'Think that' introduces a clause. 'Think in' and 'think of' are different structures with different meanings.

questions.q: I am going to discuss ______.
options: how are we encoding sensory information.
how will we encode sensory information?
questions.explanation: Embedded questions use statement word order: how we encode. The other options use question inversion, which is wrong in an embedded clause.

questions.q: In which of the following sentences, can we delete that?
options: I think that this is the end!
questions.explanation: After 'think' the conjunction 'that' can be omitted. In the other sentences 'that' is the subject and cannot be deleted.

questions.q: To make a strong recommendation, we can use the following.
options: Visual learners could make notes of all lectures.
Visual learners should make notes of all lectures.
Visual learners shall make notes of all lectures.
questions.explanation: 'Should' expresses a strong recommendation. 'Could' is weaker advice and 'shall' is for offers or future.

questions.q: She asked me if I ______ her father in London.
questions.explanation: Reported speech: present perfect or past simple becomes past perfect: had met. The other forms do not show the tense shift.

questions.q: A verb is a main sentence ______.
questions.explanation: 'Component' means part. 'Comprise' is a verb and 'campus' means a school grounds.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I think I'll have the chicken.
I'll have the chicken I think.
Have the chicken I think I'll
questions.explanation: Standard word order: I think I'll have the chicken. The other options are ungrammatical or awkwardly ordered.

questions.q: ______ you like ice-cream? How unusual!
questions.explanation: A question about a habit uses 'Do you like...?'. 'Don't' is negative and 'are' does not fit this structure.

questions.q: I've ______ in many countries during my career.
questions.explanation: Present perfect: I've lived. 'Been living' would need a duration, and 'live' is the base form.

questions.q: Don't worry. I won't tell ______.
questions.explanation: Negative sentences take 'anyone'. 'Somebody/someone' are used in positive sentences.

questions.q: That grass ______ for weeks. It looks dreadful.
questions.explanation: Present perfect passive negative: has not been cut. 'Had not being cut' is ungrammatical and 'has been cut' changes the meaning.

questions.q: I found ______ to park in the city center.
questions.explanation: 'Somewhere' means a place. 'Anywhere' is used in negatives and questions, and 'somehow' means by some means.

questions.q: She couldn't believe she ______ Brad Pitt.
questions.explanation: Past perfect for an action completed before the moment of disbelief: had seen. The other forms break the sequence.

questions.q: Do you think he'll have finished? ______.
options: Well, he should have by now
questions.explanation: 'Should have by now' is the correct short response. 'Should has' is ungrammatical and 'shouldn't' answers the wrong polarity.

questions.q: Lisa ______ an easy time at work this year.
questions.explanation: 'This year' with a continuing situation needs the present perfect: hasn't had. The other options break the tense or drop the main verb.

questions.q: The baby ______ Her life completely, I never see her nowadays.
questions.explanation: Present perfect: has taken over. 'Has took' is ungrammatical and 'taken over' lacks an auxiliary.

questions.q: 'Is Jane coming?' 'I ______. I hate her.'
questions.explanation: 'Hope not' is the correct short response to a negative outcome. 'Hope so' is positive and 'are hoping not' is ungrammatical here.

questions.q: You ______ find people driving small cars in Kuwait.
questions.explanation: 'Will not' is the correct future negative. The other options combine incompatible auxiliaries.

questions.q: Have you visited Allan's home recently? He ______ it remodeled.
questions.explanation: Causative 'has had it remodeled' means he arranged for it to be done. The other options are ungrammatical.

questions.q: Lisa was watching TV; then she ______.
