questions.explanation: Past simple after the past continuous: went out. The other options repeat the subject or use the wrong tense.

questions.q: ______? 'he's fine. He's got a new job.'
questions.explanation: 'How's Ed' asks about his condition or wellbeing. The other questions ask about appearance or personality.

questions.q: I couldn't pay. I ______ my wallet at home.
questions.explanation: Past perfect: had left (before the moment of paying). The other forms do not show the earlier action.

questions.q: It'll be good to see Ken, Won't it? ______.
options: Well, he should be by now!
questions.explanation: 'Oh, it'll be great!' agrees naturally with the tag. The other responses do not match the question.

questions.q: I ______ Ahmad about the money, I've decided he should know.
questions.explanation: 'Going to' expresses a decision already made. 'Will tell' suggests a decision made at the moment of speaking, and 'will have told' is future perfect.

questions.q: Choose the correct form.
options: Where have you seen in the zoo?
What are you seeing in the zoo?
Which animals have you seen in the zoo?
questions.explanation: 'Which animals have you seen' is the correct question. 'Where have you seen' asks about place and 'what are you seeing' is present continuous.

questions.q: Have you finished the project? ______.
questions.explanation: The present perfect short answer is 'No, I haven't'. The other answers do not match the tense of the question.

questions.q: I usually study in the evenings, but today I ______.
questions.explanation: 'Today' contrasts with the usual habit, so the present continuous: am watching. The other options are ungrammatical or use the present simple.

questions.q: A pilot ______ for many years.
questions.explanation: A singular subject takes 'has to': has to train. The other options have agreement or formation errors.

questions.q: Nora ______ to the concert.
questions.explanation: 'Want to go' is the correct form. 'Wants to goes' uses the wrong verb form and 'want' does not agree with 'Nora'.

questions.q: I ______ not think that is a good idea.
options: I don't think that's a good idea.
I do think that's a good idea
I can't think that's good idea.
questions.explanation: 'I don't think that's a good idea' is the standard negative. The other options change the meaning or omit the article.

questions.q: Emily is six years old. Her brother is nine, so he is ______.
questions.explanation: Comparing two people takes the comparative 'older'. 'Oldest' is superlative, and 'more older' is a double comparative.

questions.q: He ______ a book.
questions.explanation: An adverb ('quickly') modifies the verb: quickly reads. The other options use the wrong word class or order.

questions.q: The blackboard in my teacher's class is huge however ______ not very clean.
questions.explanation: 'It's' = it is, which fits the clause. 'It isn't' changes the meaning and 'its' is the possessive.

questions.q: Max is a ______ singer than John.
questions.explanation: 'Better' is the comparative of good. 'Gooder' is not a word and 'best' is superlative.

questions.q: I ______ out of the shower when there was a knock at the door.
questions.explanation: Past perfect for an action just completed before another past action: had just stepped. The other forms do not show the sequence.

questions.q: He is ______ to come a little late tomorrow.
questions.explanation: 'Allowed to come' means permitted to come. 'Granted' means given and 'permitted' does not take 'to' as naturally in this structure.

questions.q: The hotel was full, so I was glad that ______ in advance.
questions.explanation: Past perfect: had booked (before arriving at the hotel). The other forms do not show the earlier action.

questions.q: After they ______ the shellfish, they began to feel sick.
questions.explanation: Past perfect: had eaten (before feeling sick). The other forms do not show the earlier action.

questions.q: He said he ______ his parents.
questions.explanation: Reported speech: 'will' becomes 'would'. The other forms do not backshift the tense.

questions.q: I called his office but he ______ already left.
questions.explanation: Past perfect: had already left. 'Have' is present and 'had had' is not needed with 'left'.

questions.q: I have written this email but I have not sent it ______.
questions.explanation: 'Yet' is used in negative present perfect sentences. 'Just' and 'already' are used in positive ones.

questions.q: She promised that she would visit me ______.
questions.explanation: Reported speech shifts future time to 'the following week'. 'Previous' refers to time before the original statement.

questions.q: When she ______ in the course, she had never studied a foreign language before.
questions.explanation: Passive voice: was enrolled. The other forms change the voice or tense.

questions.q: They ______ each other since last year.
questions.explanation: 'Since' with a continuing state takes the present perfect: have known. The other forms break the tense link.

questions.q: John was stopped by the police on the way home. He ______ too fast.
questions.explanation: Past perfect continuous: had been driving (before being stopped). The other forms do not show the earlier ongoing action.

questions.q: Sally is still here. She hasn't ______ yet.
questions.explanation: Present perfect needs the past participle: hasn't gone. The other forms are not past participles.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Hey guys, check out this article, it might be useful.
Hey guys, check out this article, it might been useful
Hey guys, check out article, it might useful this.
questions.explanation: 'It might be useful' is the correct modal structure. The other options use the wrong modal form or scramble the word order.

questions.q: When I arrived at the cinema, the film ______.
questions.explanation: Past perfect: had started (before arriving). The other forms do not show the earlier action.

questions.q: Choose the correct reported speech sentence.
options: He said he finished the project the previous week
He said he has finished the project the previous week
He said he finishes the project last week
questions.explanation: Past simple in reported speech: finished the project the previous week. The other options keep the wrong tense or the wrong time word.

questions.q: We agreed ______ his proposal.
questions.explanation: 'Agree to' a proposal is the correct collocation. 'At' and 'for' do not follow 'agree' in this sense.

questions.q: Sadly, the author ______ immediately after he ______ the series.
questions.explanation: Past simple + past perfect: died after he had finished. The other options mix present and past tenses incorrectly.

questions.q: The company ______ many houses since the beginning of the year.
questions.explanation: 'Since the beginning of the year' takes the present perfect: has bought. The other forms do not link past to present.

questions.q: Laila is writing emails. She ______ emails all morning.
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous: has been writing. The other options use the wrong participle or base form.

questions.q: My hands are very dirty. I ______ my bike recently.
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous shows a recent ongoing activity with a present result: have been repairing. The other forms do not capture the ongoing recent action.

questions.q: ______ the end of the exam, we were already very tired.
questions.explanation: 'By the end' means at that point in time. 'During' and 'with' do not fit this meaning.

questions.q: The building is guarded around the clock but robberies occur ______.
questions.explanation: 'Nevertheless' means despite that. 'So' and 'therefore' express result, not contrast.

questions.q: Pizza, ______ is everyone's favorite, is the bestseller in this restaurant.
questions.explanation: A non-defining relative clause about a thing uses 'which'. 'Where' is for places and 'whose' is for possession.

questions.q: We ran ten kilometers ______ stopping.
questions.explanation: 'Without + gerund' means not doing something: without stopping. 'By' and 'after' change the meaning.

questions.q: She has been playing tennis ______ she was a child.
questions.explanation: 'Since' takes a starting point: since she was a child. 'For' takes a duration and 'from' does not fit with the present perfect here.

questions.q: What ______ for breakfast?
questions.explanation: Correct question order: do + subject + adverb + verb. The other options misplace the adverb or auxiliary.

questions.q: In this lesson, I explained the importance of ______ new vocabulary.
questions.explanation: After a preposition, use a gerund: of rehearsing. 'Rehearse' is a verb and 'rehearsal' is a noun that does not fit here.

questions.q: Do you feel ______ going out tonight?
questions.explanation: 'Feel like + gerund' means want to. 'So' and 'as' do not form this structure.

questions.q: The cat ______ under the tree.
questions.explanation: Third person singular takes 'sits'. 'Sit' does not agree and 'sitting' needs an auxiliary.

questions.q: The indirect speech of the following sentence. Tom said: 'It doesn't matter' is
options: Tom said that it didn't matter.
Tom said that he doesn't matter.
Tom said that it doesn't matter.
questions.explanation: Present simple becomes past simple: didn't matter. The other options keep the present tense or change the subject.

questions.q: All the paintings ______ in a safe place.
questions.explanation: Passive voice: are put. 'Are putting' is active and 'put' lacks the auxiliary.

questions.q: The students try to explore ______ to solve a problem together.
questions.explanation: 'Explore ways' means find methods. 'Roads' and 'knowledge' do not collocate with 'explore' in this sense.

questions.q: ______ any warning, the dog dashed to the door and barked loudly.
questions.explanation: 'Without any warning' means with no warning. 'At' and 'before' do not fit the meaning.

questions.q: The Ibrahim family live on our street. Actually, ______ house is over ______.
questions.explanation: 'Their' (possessive) + 'there' (place). The other options mix up the homophones.

questions.q: Before you submit your TMA, you ______ make sure that it is error-free.
questions.explanation: 'Should' gives a recommendation. 'Can' expresses ability and 'must' is stronger obligation than the context requires.

questions.q: If the fire alarm goes off, we ______ all leave the classroom and use the stairs.
questions.explanation: 'Should' gives a strong recommendation. 'Could' is weaker and 'can' expresses ability.

questions.q: We ______ football at school.
questions.explanation: Negative present simple with 'we' is 'don't play'. The other options have agreement or formation errors.

questions.q: The rent is due and you don't have enough money. You ______ ask your father for some money.
questions.explanation: 'Should' gives advice. 'Could' is a possibility and 'would' is conditional.

questions.q: You can use Google and search ______ the university's website.
questions.explanation: 'Search for' means try to find. 'Search on' and 'search at' do not fit this meaning.

questions.q: ______ 18, he joined the university to study engineering.
questions.explanation: 'At the age of' + number is the correct phrase. 'When' needs a clause and 'reached' needs a subject.

questions.q: You ______ exceed the speed limit.
questions.explanation: 'Mustn't' expresses prohibition. 'Shouldn't' is weaker advice and 'must' means obligation, the opposite of prohibiting.

questions.q: This year, the number of students ______ compared with last year.
questions.explanation: 'Increased' means went up and fits the comparison. 'Experiment' and 'benefit' are unrelated verbs.

questions.q: Most children ______ study on their own. They need their parents' assistance.
questions.explanation: 'Are not able to' means cannot, which fits needing help. The other options change the meaning.

questions.q: Entry to the museum is free. You ______ pay to get in.
questions.explanation: 'Don't have to' means no obligation. 'Have to' is the opposite and 'must to' is ungrammatical.

questions.q: ______ the day, she came to my office many times to ask about the raise.
questions.explanation: 'Throughout the day' means all day long. 'After' and 'on' do not fit this meaning.

questions.q: If you slept early, you ______ early.
questions.explanation: Second conditional: if + past simple, would + infinitive. The other options are the zero or third conditional forms.

questions.q: The correct question for the answer 'I have been writing them for a week' is:
options: How long have you wrote your letters?
How long have you been writing your letters?
When have you been writing your letters?
questions.explanation: The answer uses present perfect continuous, so the question must match: how long have you been writing. The other options use the wrong tense or question word.

questions.q: You have an interview tomorrow. You ______ try to rehearse common interview questions today.
questions.explanation: 'Should' gives advice. 'Can' expresses ability and 'would' is conditional.

questions.q: Engineers should ______ that fire exits are safe in case of fire.
questions.explanation: After 'should', use the base verb: ensure. The other forms do not follow a modal.

questions.q: I need to concentrate, ______ I'll have to close the door.
questions.explanation: 'So' introduces a result. 'Because' introduces a reason and 'but' introduces contrast.

questions.q: I don't feel hungry. I have ______ eaten a big sandwich.
questions.explanation: 'Just' means a moment ago. 'Since' takes a starting point and 'still' means continuing.

questions.q: People go to the university ______ they need to obtain a degree.
questions.explanation: 'Because' gives the reason. 'So that' expresses purpose and 'so' introduces a result.

questions.q: If you are sick, you ______ stay in bed.
questions.explanation: 'Should' gives advice. 'Can' expresses ability and 'could' is a possibility.

questions.q: Junk food is very unhealthy. You ______ eat a lot of it.
questions.explanation: 'Shouldn't' advises against doing something. 'Should' is the opposite and 'can' expresses ability.

questions.q: He ______ email before, so I showed him how to use it.
questions.explanation: Present perfect negative with 'he': has not used. 'Have' does not agree with 'he' and 'has used' is positive.

questions.q: Which is correct?
options: He studied very hard, so he got the highest mark
He studied very hard, he got the highest mark, so
He studied very hard because he gets the highest mark.
questions.explanation: 'So' correctly links cause and result. The other options misplace the conjunction or mix tenses.

questions.q: He asked if he could borrow my pen.
questions.explanation: The reported question structure is correct: asked if he could. No change is needed.

questions.q: This cat is going to ______ a car one day.
questions.explanation: Future passive: be killed by. The other options are ungrammatical or active.

questions.q: I am learning French, but I haven't been ______ for long.
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous: haven't been learning. The other forms do not follow 'been' in this structure.

questions.q: I ______ overtime for the past six months.
questions.explanation: 'For the past six months' takes the present perfect: have worked. The other forms do not link past to present.

questions.q: We need to ______ to finish this project on time.
questions.explanation: After 'to', use the base verb: collaborate. 'Collaboration' is a noun and 'collaborating' does not follow 'to' here.

questions.q: This semester, we ______ the library.
questions.explanation: Present perfect for a completed action within the semester: have activated. The other forms are continuous or non-finite.

questions.q: Which option is the right reported speech sentence?
options: She told me that she had visited Paris
I have visited Paris, she told me
She told me that she visits Paris
questions.explanation: Past simple becomes past perfect in reported speech: had visited. The other options keep the wrong tense or scramble the order.

questions.q: It's raining. The rain started two hours ago. It ______ for two hours.
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous: has been raining. The other options use the wrong participle or auxiliary.

questions.q: She told me she is studying for the quiz.
questions.explanation: Incorrect — 'is studying' should be backshifted to 'was studying' in reported speech. So the sentence is grammatically incorrect.

questions.q: Which sentence correctly uses the present perfect simple tense?
options: We have seen that movie three times.
She is eating lunch when the phone rang.
They have visited Paris last summer
questions.explanation: Present perfect with 'three times' is correct. The second mixes tenses and the third uses present perfect with a finished past time.

questions.q: She ______ in China before she went to Thailand.
questions.explanation: Past perfect: had lived (before going to Thailand). The other forms do not show the earlier action.

questions.q: I have lived in London ______ five years.
questions.explanation: 'For' takes a period of time: for five years. 'Since' takes a starting point and 'ago' refers to a past point.

questions.q: First, we ate at the cafeteria. Then, we went to class. Which is the correct complex sentence?
options: After we had eaten at the cafeteria, we went to class
After we ate at the cafeteria, we went to class
After we ate at the cafeteria, we had gone to class
questions.explanation: Past perfect + past simple shows the sequence: after we had eaten, we went. The other options lose the sequence.

questions.q: I didn't know much about the topic, so I had to ______ information.
questions.explanation: 'Look up' means search for information. 'Look at' means view and 'look to' means rely on.

questions.q: She ______ out through the window since she heard the bad news.
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous with 'since': has been looking. 'Have' does not agree with 'she' and 'has looked' does not fit the continuing action.

questions.q: What ______ this weekend?
questions.explanation: Present continuous for future plans: are you doing. The other options are ungrammatical or not a question.

questions.q: My granny ______ my little sister for the past two days.
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous: has been looking after. The other options use the simple or passive form, which do not fit the ongoing action.

questions.q: I am busy right now. I ______ breakfast.
questions.explanation: Present continuous for an action happening now: am having. The other options are the base verb or gerund.

questions.q: In Britain, you ______ drive when you are 17.
questions.explanation: 'Can' expresses permission. 'Allow' needs a subject and 'would' is conditional.

questions.q: Clients ______ me recently.
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous for recent repeated actions: have been visiting. The other forms do not capture the recent ongoing pattern.

questions.q: I forgot ______ her the message.
questions.explanation: 'Forget to do' means fail to do a task: forgot to give. 'Forget doing' means not remember a past action.

questions.q: I learnt how ______ when I was very young.
questions.explanation: 'Learn how to' takes the to-infinitive: how to swim. The other forms do not follow this structure.

questions.q: I've forgotten how ______ this machine.
questions.explanation: 'Forget how to' takes the to-infinitive: how to use. The other forms do not follow this structure.

questions.q: Did you remember ______ that library book back?
questions.explanation: 'Remember to do' means remember a task: to take. 'Remember doing' means recall a past action, which does not fit here.

questions.q: Remind me ______ him when we get home.
questions.explanation: 'Remind someone to do' takes the to-infinitive: to call. The other forms do not follow this structure.

questions.q: What did you learn ______ in the last lecture?
questions.explanation: 'Learn about' means gain knowledge on a topic. 'Learn of' means hear about and 'learn to' needs a verb.

questions.q: I prefer tea ______ coffee.
questions.explanation: 'Prefer A to B' is the correct structure. 'Over' and 'than' do not follow 'prefer' in this pattern.

questions.q: By the time the lesson starts, I ______ my notes.
questions.explanation: Future perfect: will have reviewed (completed before a future time). The other forms do not express completion before a future point.
